title: The AI Researcher
answer: Ten areas where artificial intelligence is changing research and teaching: literature review, citation mapping, quantitative and qualitative analysis, grants, writing and peer review, course design, research data, the laboratory, and the integrity rules that govern all of it.

sections.body: Artificial intelligence is now a working part of the research cycle, not a future promise. In literature review, tools scan and summarize large bodies of papers, extract claims, and group studies by theme. Citation mapping software traces how ideas move between papers and finds related work that keyword search misses. Quantitative analysis uses AI for data cleaning, statistical modeling, and code generation, while qualitative analysis uses it to code interviews and detect patterns in text. Grant writing, peer review, course design, research data management, and laboratory work all have AI tools that draft, check, organize, or simulate parts of the process. Governance and integrity tools monitor for plagiarism, data fabrication, and undisclosed AI use.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Literature search and summarization are the most mature, producing useful first drafts of evidence maps, but they still miss relevant studies and can misstate findings. Citation mapping is reliable in well indexed fields but weak in the humanities and non English sources. Quantitative and qualitative analysis both benefit from AI assisted coding and data cleaning, yet the models can generate plausible but wrong code or shallow themes. Grant and peer review tools improve clarity and catch errors, but they do not assess novelty or ethical risk. Laboratory automation handles repetitive tasks like liquid handling and image analysis, while full autonomous discovery remains out of reach, and the honest limit across all ten areas is that AI produces drafts, suggestions, and flags, not finished scholarship.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis, which shows how AI gathers and summarizes sources, then move to Citation Mapping and Discovery to see how those sources connect. Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods cover the two main analytical traditions, with the former focused on code, statistics, and replication and the latter on text, interviews, and interpretation. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review address the written products of research, from seeking money to publishing results. Course Design and Teaching and Research Data and Repositories shift to the academic environment, covering how AI changes instruction and how data is stored and shared. Laboratory Automation and Simulation describes physical and computational experiments, while Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity sets the rules that apply to all the other pages. The site's library of 135 research papers and 11,075 extracted claims sits behind these pages, and every link goes to the original paper rather than a search tool.
